5.17pm It was a very calm knock from an experienced Shakib, and he eventually takes 
his side home. Not dissimilar to MS Dhoni's finishing: never fussed for boundaries, 
happy to keep rotating the strike when required and finding gaps for crucial runs to 
complete the chase. He finishes just four short of a hundred, but will be pleased to have 
done the job. 
Jack: "Zimbabwe only have themselves to blame with this loss after giving away all 
those wides." 
Shapla: "Everyone talking about Shakib while Saifuddin made a good contribution " 
Time for the presentations 
Here's Taylor after a close loss for his side: "Much improved performance, but 
Bangladesh didn't look like panicking and held their nerve. There are fine lines you talk 
about.. hope the last game goes our way." 
Shakib is the Player of the Match for his 2 for 42 and 96*: "Today was the day I had to 
put my hands up. Very happy... Lot of credit to Saifuddin, he showed a lot of composure. 
Today the wicket was slower. If the bowlers were bowling straight into the wicket, you 
had to take chances, which is where we lost wickets." 
Tamim, the winning captain: "Restricting them to 240 was a decent job by the bowlers. 
We definitely had some plans, and as a batting team, we could have done better. They 
way Shakib and Saifuddin batted was nice to see." 
joynul: "Experience, the difference between these two teams today was just Experience." 
An exciting finish in the end. The experience of Shakib and the maturity of Saifuddin 
made all the difference, but don't forget the four wickets by Shoriful, which helped 
restrict Zimbabwe to 240. And the hosts - like in the Test and the first ODI - had their 
moments, but couldn't capitalise on them. Too many extras didn't help either. But 
anyway, catch us for the final game with Zimbabwe seeking crucial Super League 
points, if not the series. Until then, it's a goodbye from Chandan, Ranjith, Sreshth and 
me, Himanshu!
